mainTopic: Withdrawing from a נדה and separating near the וסת, and the difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא on knowing the source of one's טומאה
overview: The amud opens by explaining why the 'long way vs. short way' rule for someone impure in the מקדש has no match for a נדה: the two cases work in opposite directions. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן then raises an apparent contradiction between two statements of אביי, and the גמרא answers that 'liable for two' was a general ruling, not one about our משנה. Next, the גמרא asks for the Torah source that a man must not withdraw immediately when his wife becomes impure during relations. חזקיה brings an עשה, and רב פפא brings a לא תעשה from 'לא תקרב'. A ברייתא teaches that a man must separate from his wife close to her וסת, and רבה sets this at one עונה. Several אמוראים then teach the punishment for ignoring this and the rewards of separating, of making הבדלה on wine, and of holy conduct, all learned from neighboring פסוקים. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks how רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא differ. חזקיה and עולא say the difference is a person who knew he was טמא but not whether it was from a שרץ or a נבלה. עולא answers a contradiction in רבי אליעזר's words from the wording of the פסוקים, and the גמרא begins to explain רבי עקיבא's reading, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But the rule was only taught about the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the long-way/short-way distinction appears in the משנה only for the מקדש, not for נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned this distinction only in the case of the מקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the 'long way vs. short way' rule also applies to a נדה. The משנה only taught it for someone impure in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the same distinction applied to נדה, the משנה would have said so there too. Since it mentions the distinction only for the מקדש, the גמרא needs to explain why נדה is different. This sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: But we learned it regarding the Temple!
phrases.notes: He means the 'long way or short way out' rule, which the משנה teaches only for someone who became impure inside the מקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנַן בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the earlier discussion (before this section) about applying the long/short-way distinction to נדה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the long/short-way distinction also applies to נדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה states the distinction only for the מקדש, which implies it does not exist for נדה.

steps.title: The two cases do not line up
steps.stepSummary: There is no matching distinction because 'long' and 'short' work in opposite ways in the two cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because the cases are not similar. The long way here is like the short way there, and the long way there is like the short way here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה gives no long/short distinction for נדה. The two cases simply do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדה, the 'longer' path is to wait until the body relaxes and then withdraw. That is the proper, exempt way, so it matches the 'short' (exempt) way out of the מקדש. The 'long' (liable) path in the מקדש matches the quick, improper withdrawal with a נדה. So the labels flip, and no single rule covers both.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'long' always means liable. With a נדה, the longer path of waiting is the correct and exempt one. That is exactly why the two cases cannot be compared.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because they are not similar;
the long way here is the short way there,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the נדה case and 'there' means the מקדש case.

phrases.english: and the long way there is the short way here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by explaining the משנה's silence about נדה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (the cases are structurally different)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the long/short distinction should apply to נדה just as it does to the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such distinction exists for נדה, because 'long' and 'short' play reversed roles in the two cases.

steps.title: Two statements of אביי seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן objects: calling the man an אנוס assumes it was not near her וסת, but making him liable for two offerings assumes it was near her וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן objected: Did אביי really say he is an אנוס (forced by circumstances)? That means we are talking about a time not close to her expected period. But אביי also said he is liable for two sin-offerings. That means we are dealing with a time close to her expected period!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges אביי by showing that two of his statements assume opposite cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the man an אנוס makes sense only if her period came unexpectedly, far from her וסת, so he could not have known. Making him liable for two חטאת offerings (one for entering and one for withdrawing) means he counts as a שוגג, which fits only if it was near her וסת and he should have been careful. Both statements cannot describe the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: One forced by circumstances beyond his control (exempt)
Near her expected time of menstruation

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan objected to it:
Did Abaye say, 'he is a victim of circumstance'?
phrases.notes: This is what אביי said about the man in our משנה who waits and then withdraws.

phrases.english: Evidently we are speaking of a time not near her expected period?!
But Abaye is the one who said he is liable for two,
evidently we are dealing with a time near her expected period!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new issue: the consistency of אביי's statements about the same topic.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's two statements: 'he is an אנוס' and 'he is liable for two'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first statement requires a case far from her וסת, and the second requires a case near her וסת. They seem to describe the same case, so they contradict.

steps.title: The second statement was a general ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי's 'liable for two' was said as a separate, general ruling and not about our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי's statement was said, it was said in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The two statements of אביי are about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'אנוס' statement refers to the משנה's case, which is far from her וסת. The 'liable for two' statement was a separate ruling about someone who had relations near her וסת. Since they describe different situations, they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: In general (not about this specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי calls the man an אנוס in the משנה's case, which is far from her וסת. His ruling of 'liable for two' is a separate rule for a case near her וסת.

phrases.english: When that statement of Abaye was said,
phrases.notes: He means the 'liable for two' statement.

phrases.english: it was said in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּאַבָּיֵי בְּעָלְמָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different contexts (the statements refer to different cases)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to refer to the משנה's case, which created a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Liable for two' is a general ruling for a case near her וסת. The משנה's case is far from her וסת, so there the man is an אנוס.

steps.title: Where does the Torah forbid relations with a נדה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן יוסי בן לקוניא asks רבי שמעון בן יוסי בן לקוניא for the Torah source of the prohibition against relations with a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן יוסי בן לקוניא asked רבי שמעון בן יוסי בן לקוניא: From where in the Torah do we know the prohibition against one who has relations with a נדה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins with a question asking for the Torah source of the prohibition against relations with a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אזהרה is a formal Torah warning, and it is needed before someone can be punished. The question asks which פסוק provides that warning for relations with a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has relations with a menstruating woman

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosei ben Lakonya asked

phrases.aramaic: מֵרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא:
phrases.english: of Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei ben Lakonya:
the warning for one who has relations with a menstruating woman,
from where is it in the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: the Torah source for the נדה prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah verse that serves as the אזהרה for relations with a נדה.

steps.title: A clod thrown and an obvious verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוסי בן לקוניא throws a clod at him and quotes the clear פסוק forbidding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took a clod of earth and threw it at him, saying: The warning for one who has relations with a נדה? 'And to a woman in her impure state of נדה you shall not come close'!
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered with a rebuke. The source is an explicit פסוק, so there is no need to search for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing the clod shows that the questioner should have known this, because the פסוק states the prohibition openly. 'Do not come close' is the direct Torah warning against relations with a נדה.
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah warning against relations with a נדה is the פסוק 'ואל אשה בנדת טמאתה לא תקרב' in ויקרא 18:19.

phrases.english: He took a clod and threw it at him:
A warning for one who has relations with a menstruating woman?!
'And to a woman in her impurity of menstruation
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:19

phrases.english: you shall not come close'!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקַל קָלָא פְּתַק בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The explicit פסוק in ויקרא 18:19, 'ואל אשה בנדת טמאתה לא תקרב'.

steps.title: What was really being asked: the source for not withdrawing right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question was not about the basic נדה prohibition, which is obvious. It was about the case in the משנה: where do we learn that he must not withdraw immediately?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is what was meant: a man is having relations with a pure woman and she tells him 'I have become impure.' Where do we learn the warning that he must not pull away right away?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets רבי יונתן's question so it makes sense after the clod-throwing. This sets up the next steps, which bring the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain prohibition of a נדה is written clearly, which is why רבי שמעון threw a clod. So the question must have been about something less obvious: how to separate when she becomes impure in the middle. The משנה's rule that he may not withdraw immediately needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It explains what the question in Step 5 really meant, since the simple prohibition did not need asking.

phrases.english: Rather, the warning for one who was having relations with a pure woman
and she said to him: 'I have become impure,'
that he must not withdraw immediately: from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַזְהָרָה לִמְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם הַטְּהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reframes the question of Step 5 in light of the answer in Step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a man must not withdraw immediately when his wife becomes impure during relations

steps.title: חזקיה: 'her impurity shall be upon him'
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from the פסוק that even once she is נדה, he should remain 'upon her' and not pull away at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: the פסוק says 'and her impurity shall be upon him.' This means even at the time of her impurity, he should stay upon her.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question with a פסוק that tells the man to stay where he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'shall be upon him' are read as an instruction for the moment she becomes נדה. He should not pull out right away. This source is worded as something to do, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Her state of impurity as a נדה

phrases.english: חזקיה said: the verse says:
'and her impurity shall be upon him'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24

phrases.english: even at the time of her impurity, she shall be 'upon him.'
phrases.notes: He means the man stays in place even once she becomes impure, rather than pulling out at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'her impurity shall be upon him' teach that he should not withdraw immediately

steps.title: We have a positive command, but where is the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that חזקיה's source is only a positive command (עשה). It asks for a source that makes it a prohibition (לא תעשה).
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a positive command. Where do we learn a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts חזקיה's source but asks for more. It wants a 'don't' command, not only a 'do' command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original question asked for an אזהרה, a warning, which usually means a לא תעשה. חזקיה's פסוק only tells him what to do. So the גמרא looks for a negative command.

phrases.english: We have found a positive command;
a prohibition, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן עֲשֵׂה, לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 8 and asks for a stronger kind of source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A negative-command source for not withdrawing immediately

steps.title: רב פפא: 'Do not approach' also means 'do not withdraw'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings 'לא תקרב' and shows from ישעיהו that the root קרב can also mean moving away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the פסוק says 'Do not approach.' 'Do not approach' also means 'do not withdraw,' as it is written: 'Those who say, Keep to yourself, do not come near me, for I am holier than you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא supplies the prohibition. He reads the word 'approach' as also covering pulling away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו, 'קרב אליך' means 'move back to yourself,' so the root קרב can mean withdrawing. That lets 'לא תקרב' forbid both coming close to a נדה and pulling away the wrong way. Now there is a לא תעשה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not approach (the prohibition of a נדה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for not withdrawing immediately when a woman becomes נדה during relations: an עשה from חזקיה ('ותהי נדתה עליו') and a לא תעשה from רב פפא ('לא תקרב').

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״לֹא תִקְרַב״;
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: the verse says: 'Do not approach';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:19

phrases.english: 'Do not approach' also means 'do not withdraw,'
as it is written: 'Those who say: Keep back to yourself,'
'do not come near me, for I am holier than you.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 65:5. Here the same word קרב means moving away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אָמַר קְרָא: לֹא תִקְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא תקרב' also means 'do not withdraw,' as the root קרב can mean moving away (ישעיהו 65:5)

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: separate from your wife close to her expected period
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יאשיה learns from 'and you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity' that a man must separate from his wife near her וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity.' רבי יאשיה said: from here comes a warning to Jews to separate from their wives close to their expected period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about separating before the expected period. This connects to the earlier discussion about being near her וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the topic was a woman who became impure during relations. Now the rule moves earlier in time. Even before she sees blood, the couple must separate when her period is expected.

keyTerms.meaning: The expected time of a woman's period

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:31

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה: מִיכָּן אַזְהָרָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya said: from here is a warning to the children of Israel
that they must separate from their wives close to their expected period.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְהִזַּרְתֶּם אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִטֻּמְאָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: separating before the expected period
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a Torah warning to separate from one's wife close to her וסת

steps.title: How long before her period?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much time before the וסת the couple must separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact length of time 'close to her period' means. This sets up רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Close to' is vague. The גמרא wants a set amount of time so the rule can be kept.

phrases.english: And how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the length of time in Step 11's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of time before the וסת that one must separate

steps.title: רבה: one עונה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that one must separate for one עונה, meaning the daytime or the night in which her period is expected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: one עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the set time: one עונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is half of a full day, either a daytime or a night. So the couple separates for the daytime or night when her period is expected.

keyTerms.meaning: A time period of a daytime or a night

steps.whatToRemember: One must separate from one's wife for one עונה (a day or a night) at the time her period is expected.

phrases.english: Rabba said: one עונה.
phrases.notes: An עונה is either a daytime or a night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: עוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One עונה, which is a daytime or a night

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: the danger of not separating near her period
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: a man who does not separate near her וסת risks the death of his sons, even if they are as great as בני אהרן. He learns this from the closeness of the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: anyone who does not separate from his wife close to her period, even if he has sons like the sons of אהרן, they die. As it is written: 'And you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity... and of her who is unwell with her impurity,' and right after it: 'After the death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a strong warning about how serious this rule is. The proof comes from the order of the פסוקים in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section about separating from a נדה ends in ויקרא 15, and the very next פסוק begins 'After the death of the two sons of אהרן.' רבי שמעון בן יוחאי reads this closeness as a hint: ignoring the separation leads to death of one's children.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is unwell, during her period
And right next to it (in the Torah)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously חז"ל treated separating near the וסת. They tied it to a punishment hinted at by the order of the Torah's פסוקים.
steps.whatToRemember: Separating near the וסת is a real Torah warning (רבי יאשיה). It lasts one עונה (רבה), and ignoring it brings a severe punishment (רבי שמעון בן יוחאי).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ פּוֹרֵשׁ מֵאִשְׁתּוֹ סָמוּךְ לְוִסְתָּהּ,
phrases.english: anyone who does not separate from his wife close to her expected period,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הוֹיִין לוֹ בָּנִים כִּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן – מֵתִים;
phrases.english: even if he has sons like the sons of Aharon, they die;
as it is written: 'And you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity'
'and of her who is unwell in her impurity,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:31–33, the end of the section about a נדה.

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'After the death.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:1, which goes on to mention the death of the two sons of אהרן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a warning about the punishment for breaking the rule taught in Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who does not separate from his wife near her וסת risks the death of his sons, learned from 'אחרי מות' coming right after the נדה section

steps.title: Separating near the expected period brings male children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a man who separates from his wife near her וסת will have sons. He learns it from the closeness of two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who separates from his wife near her expected period will have male children. It says 'to separate between the impure and the pure,' and right next to it, 'If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a positive reward for keeping the separation it just discussed. Separating near the וסת brings sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 gave the punishment for not separating. This step gives the reward for separating. The proof comes from two neighboring פסוקים: the end of one chapter speaks about separating, and the next chapter opens with giving birth to a boy.

keyTerms.meaning: close to the time her period is expected
and right next to it (a lesson from neighboring פסוקים)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא learns ideas from the order of פסוקים, a method used again in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who separates from his wife close to her expected period
will have male children,
as it is written: 'To separate between the impure and the pure,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:47, the last פסוק of the chapter.

phrases.english: and right next to it:
'If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2. It opens the very next chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כׇּל הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵאִשְׁתּוֹ סָמוּךְ לְוִסְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the reward for separating, after Step 14 gave the punishment for not separating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who separates near the וסת will have sons, learned from the closeness of ויקרא 11:47 and 12:2.

steps.title: A different reward: sons fit to teach Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the reward is sons who are worthy to teach הלכה, learned from 'to separate' and 'to teach' in one פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: He will have sons worthy of teaching הלכה, as it says 'to separate... and to teach.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reward for the same act of separating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן used the neighboring chapter about giving birth. רבי יהושע בן לוי uses a different פסוק, where 'to separate' is followed right away by 'and to teach.' So the reward is sons who can give rulings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
He will have sons worthy of teaching (giving rulings),
as it is written: 'To separate... and to teach.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:10–11. The dots skip the middle words, so 'to separate' leads straight into 'to teach.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר הוֹיִין לוֹ בָּנִים רְאוּיִין לְהוֹרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reward than רבי יוחנן for the same act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who separates near the וסת will have sons fit for הוראה.

steps.title: Making הבדלה on wine brings male children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that one who makes הבדלה on wine on מוצאי שבת will have sons. The word 'להבדיל' connects הבדלה to the פסוק next to the birth of a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who makes הבדלה on wine on מוצאי שבת will have male children. It says 'to separate between the holy and the ordinary,' and elsewhere it says 'to separate between the impure and the pure,' and right next to that, 'If a woman conceives.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same style of drashah for a new act: making הבדלה over wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הבדלה separates holy from ordinary, which matches 'to separate between the holy and the ordinary.' That same word 'to separate' also appears in the פסוק that sits next to 'If a woman conceives.' So the same reward of sons applies.

keyTerms.meaning: one who makes הבדלה over wine
and it is written there (in another place)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק 'between the impure and the pure' appears twice: once in ויקרא 10:10 and once in 11:47. The link to giving birth comes from the second one, which sits right before chapter 12.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who makes havdala over wine
at the end of Shabbatot
will have male children;
as it is written: 'To separate between the holy and the ordinary,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:10

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַטָּמֵא וּבֵין הַטָּהוֹר״,
phrases.english: and it is written there: 'To separate between the impure and the pure,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:47. The same word 'to separate' shows up again here.

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'If a woman conceives.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמַּבְדִּיל עַל הַיַּיִן בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת הוֹיִין לוֹ בָּנִים זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same neighboring-פסוקים method to a new act, הבדלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who makes הבדלה on wine on מוצאי שבת will have sons.

steps.title: For הבדלה too: sons fit to teach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי again says the reward is sons worthy of teaching הלכה, from 'to separate... and to teach.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Sons worthy of teaching הלכה, as it says 'to separate... and to teach.'
steps.whatsHappening: As in Step 16, רבי יהושע בן לוי gives his own version of the reward, this time for הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'to separate' fits even more directly, because the same פסוק says 'between the holy and the ordinary,' which is exactly what הבדלה does. Right after it comes 'and to teach,' so the reward is sons who teach.
steps.whatToRemember: For both separating near the וסת and making הבדלה, רבי יוחנן says the reward is sons, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says it is sons fit to teach.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Sons worthy of teaching (giving rulings),
as it is written: 'To separate... and to teach.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר בָּנִים רְאוּיִן לְהוֹרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative reward for הבדלה, matching his view in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who makes הבדלה on wine will have sons fit for הוראה.

steps.title: Holy conduct during intimacy brings male children
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that one who acts with holiness during marital relations will have sons, learned from 'You shall sanctify yourselves,' which is near 'If a woman conceives.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Anyone who sanctifies himself during marital relations will have male children. It says 'You shall sanctify yourselves and be holy,' and near it, 'If a woman conceives.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third teaching in the same style: being holy and modest during relations brings sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the linking פסוק is about holiness, not separating. It also sits near the opening of the chapter about giving birth, so the same reward of sons is learned.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of marital relations

steps.whatToRemember: Three acts (separating near the וסת, הבדלה on wine, holy conduct) are all tied to the reward of sons through פסוקים near 'If a woman conceives.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who sanctifies himself
phrases.notes: He means acting with modesty and holiness.

phrases.english: at the time of marital relations
will have male children;
as it is said: 'You shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:44

phrases.english: and near it: 'If a woman conceives.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כׇּל הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁעַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third act learned with the same neighboring-פסוקים method, closing this aggadic section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sanctifies himself during relations will have sons.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what is the difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's words in the משנה about 'the שרץ and it is hidden from him' and asks what practical difference separates him from רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'The שרץ, and it is hidden from him,' and so on. What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side topic and goes back to the משנה. It quotes רבי אליעזר's source and asks how his view differs from רבי עקיבא's. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, both רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא agree that a קרבן עולה ויורד is brought only for forgetting the טומאה, not for forgetting the מקדש or the קדשים. They just learn it from different words. So the גמרא asks what practical difference comes out of their two sources.

keyTerms.meaning: a creeping creature that makes things impure
and it was hidden from him (he forgot)
etc.; the quote continues as in the משנה
what is the difference between them?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not asking what the הלכה is. Both תנאים agree on the הלכה. The question is what practical difference their different sources create.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
'The creeping creature, and it is hidden from him,' etc.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2. We're back in the משנה. 'Etc.' points to the rest of it, including רבי עקיבא's view.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ וְנֶעְלַם מִמֶּנּוּ כּוּ׳ מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic section and goes back to the משנה's dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Since רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא reach the same הלכה from different words of the פסוק, what practical difference is there between them?

steps.title: חזקיה: the difference is not knowing whether it was a שרץ or a נבלה
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is a person who knew he became טמא but did not know if it was from a שרץ or a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: the difference between them is a case of a שרץ or a נבלה. רבי אליעזר holds that the person must know whether he became טמא from a שרץ or from a נבלה. רבי עקיבא holds that he does not need to know this. Since he knows that he became טמא in general, it does not matter whether it came from a שרץ or a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20 by giving a case where רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא would rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the person must first have known about his טומאה before he forgot it. They argue about how much he had to know. For רבי אליעזר, he must know the exact source, a שרץ or a נבלה. For רבי עקיבא, knowing 'I became טמא' is enough to make him liable for a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping animal (like a mouse) whose dead body makes a person טמא
An animal that died without proper שחיטה, which also makes a person טמא
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree the person knew he was טמא. The only question is whether he also had to know WHICH kind of טומאה it was.

phrases.english: Hizkiyah said:
A creeping animal or a carcass is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means a person who isn't sure which of the two made him טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
We require that he know
whether he became impure from a creeping animal
or he became impure from a carcass;
and Rabbi Akiva holds:
We do not require that he know,
since he knows that he became impure in general,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word and some have the square-bracket word. Both mean 'that he became impure.'

phrases.english: it is not necessary whether he became impure from a creeping animal
or he became impure from a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר חזקיה: שרץ ונבלה איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 20 about the practical difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person who knew he was טמא but not whether it came from a שרץ or a נבלה. רבי אליעזר requires knowing the source; רבי עקיבא does not.

steps.title: עולא agrees, and he reached this through a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives the same answer as חזקיה. The גמרא explains that he did not say it outright. It came out of a contradiction he raised in רבי אליעזר's words and then answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא also said: the difference between them is a case of a שרץ or a נבלה. This is because עולא pointed out a contradiction between one statement of רבי אליעזר and another, and then resolved it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that עולא agrees with חזקיה. It also tells us how he got there: through a contradiction and its answer, which the גמרא is about to lay out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup line. The words 'רמי... ומשני' tell us a contradiction (the next step) and then an answer (later) are coming. עולא's view about שרץ ונבלה will turn out to be built into that answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: And so too said Ulla:
A creeping animal or a carcass is the difference between them.
For Ulla raises a contradiction
of Rabbi Eliezer against Rabbi Eliezer,
and resolves it –

steps.triggerLanguage: וכן אמר עולא: שרץ ונבלה איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second אמורא who agrees with חזקיה, and sets up עולא's contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא also holds that the difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is the case of not knowing whether one's טומאה came from a שרץ or a נבלה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר seems to say elsewhere that a person is liable either way
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks: does רבי אליעזר really require knowing the exact source? In a ברייתא he says that a person who knows he sinned but not which sin he did is liable either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אליעזר really say that we require him to know whether he became טמא from a שרץ or from a נבלה? But a ברייתא contradicts this. רבי אליעזר says: whichever way you look at it, he is liable. If he ate חלב, he is liable. If he ate נותר, he is liable. If he broke שבת, he is liable. If he broke יום הכפורים, he is liable. If he was with his wife who is a נדה, he is liable. If he was with his sister, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא challenges the idea that רבי אליעזר demands exact knowledge. He brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר makes a person bring a קרבן even when he does not know which of two sins he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the person knows he did something forbidden but is unsure which prohibition it was. רבי אליעזר still makes him liable, because either way he sinned. That seems to clash with רבי אליעזר's demand in our משנה that the person know whether his טומאה came from a שרץ or a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (from another source)
Whichever way you look at it
Meat of a קרבן left over past its allowed time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as a person who did all six sins. Each pair is one act where he does not know which of the two it was.

phrases.english: Does Rabbi Eliezer say
we require that he know

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּשֶׁרֶץ אִיטַּמִּי אִי בִּנְבֵלָה אִיטַּמִּי?!
phrases.english: whether he became impure from a creeping animal or he became impure from a carcass?!
And they contrasted it: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Whichever way you look at it:
phrases.notes: The case is someone who did one forbidden act but can't tell which of two prohibitions it broke.

phrases.english: If he ate forbidden fat – he is liable;
if he ate leftover sacrificial meat – he is liable;
if he desecrated Shabbat – he is liable;
if he desecrated Yom Kippur – he is liable;
if he was with his wife while she was a niddah – he is liable;
if he was with his sister – he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: מי אמר רבי אליעזר בעינן עד דידע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the contradiction that עולא raises, as announced in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (from Step 21) that רבי אליעזר requires knowing the exact source of the טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר makes a person liable without knowing exactly which sin he did ('מה נפשך'). So why should he demand exact knowledge of שרץ or נבלה?

steps.title: רבי יהושע: he must know exactly what he sinned with
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי יהושע answers רבי אליעזר with a פסוק that teaches the sinner must know exactly how he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: the פסוק says, 'Or his sin in which he sinned is made known to him.' This means he is not liable until it is known to you exactly how he sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with רבי יהושע's reply. He is the one who demands exact knowledge, and he takes it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the contradiction even sharper. In the ברייתא, it is רבי יהושע who requires knowing the exact sin, while רבי אליעזר rejects that requirement. Yet in our משנה, רבי אליעזר is the one demanding exact knowledge of שרץ or נבלה. עולא's answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is made known to him

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the two sources side by side. רבי אליעזר seems lenient about knowing details in the ברייתא but strict in our משנה. עולא's answer will have to explain the difference.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
Behold, it says:
"Or it is made known to him
his sin in which he sinned" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:23

phrases.english: until it is known to you in what he sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לו רבי יהושע, הרי הוא אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in Step 23. It shows that רבי יהושע, not רבי אליעזר, is the one who requires exact knowledge there, which sharpens עולא's contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: there is no liability for a קרבן חטאת until the sinner knows exactly which sin he did, based on 'או הודע אליו חטאתו אשר חטא בה'.

steps.title: עולא explains why טומאה is different from a regular sin
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers his own contradiction. For a חטאת, the פסוק shows that any sin is enough. For טומאה, the extra words 'or the carcass of an impure שרץ' show that he must have known the exact source of his טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא answers: There, the Torah said 'in which he sinned, he shall bring', so any sin at all is enough. Here, since the פסוק already wrote 'any impure thing', why do I need 'or the carcass of an impure שרץ'? Learn from this that we need him to know whether he became טמא from a שרץ or from a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא resolves the contradiction he raised in רבי אליעזר. He shows that the two cases come from different פסוקים, and each פסוק is worded differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a חטאת, the פסוק only says 'in which he sinned', so knowing that he did some sin is enough. For טומאה, the פסוק first says 'any impure thing', which already includes everything. Naming a שרץ on its own is therefore extra, and רבי אליעזר learns from it that he must have known exactly what made him טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And he answers. Here עולא resolves his own question.
Literally 'the Merciful One'. It means the Torah.
Any sin at all. The exact sin does not need to be known.
Why do I need it? This points to words in a פסוק that seem extra.
Learn from it. This introduces the lesson drawn from those extra words.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, a חטאת needs only the knowledge that some sin was done. טומאה is different, because the extra word שרץ requires knowing the exact source of the טומאה. This is the practical difference between him and רבי עקיבא that חזקיה and עולא described.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two פסוקים. 'אשר חטא' is about a regular חטאת. 'בכל דבר טמא' and 'בנבלת שרץ' are about the person who became טמא and entered the מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that רבי אליעזר's two rulings do not contradict each other. Each one comes from the wording of a different פסוק.

phrases.english: And he resolves it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is עולא, answering the contradiction he raised himself.

phrases.english: There, "in which he sinned, he shall bring"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:23

phrases.english: the Torah said, meaning any sin at all.
Here, since it is written "any impure thing",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2

phrases.english: why do I need "or the carcass of an impure שרץ"?
Learn from it: we need him to know

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּשֶׁרֶץ אִיטַּמִּי אִי בִּנְבֵלָה אִיטַּמִּי.
phrases.english: whether he became טמא from a שרץ or became טמא from a נבלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: הָתָם, ״אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וְהֵבִיא״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 23, where רבי אליעזר holds a sinner is liable even without knowing which sin he did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases based on the wording of different פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אליעזר does not require knowing the exact sin for a חטאת, he should not require knowing the exact source of טומאה either.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a חטאת, 'אשר חטא' means any sin is enough. For טומאה, the extra words 'בנבלת שרץ' require knowing the exact source.

steps.title: How does רבי עקיבא explain the extra words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא does with the words 'or the carcass of an impure שרץ', since he does not learn רבי אליעזר's lesson from them. The answer begins with the word 'since'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? He holds that since...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא explains the extra words that רבי אליעזר learned from. It is setting up an answer that starts here with 'since' and continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not require knowing whether the טומאה came from a שרץ or a נבלה. So he needs a different reason why the Torah mentions a שרץ separately. The word אַיְּידֵי hints that he sees the extra words as said along with something else, and not as a separate lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, or because it was already. This often means words were written along with other words and do not teach something new.

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא, what does he do with these words?
Since...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – אַיְּידֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how רבי אליעזר learns from the extra words, the גמרא turns to how רבי עקיבא reads them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי עקיבא explain the extra phrase 'בנבלת שרץ טמא' if he does not learn from it that one must know the exact source of the טומאה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with 'אַיְּידֵי' (since) and continues after this point.
